destination.name: Yunnan
destination.pitch: Twelve days buys the whole climb from 1,400 m rice terraces to a 3,300 m Tibetan town, and the walking between the old towns is worth far more than the old towns themselves.

because.nature: The Honghe Hani terraces drop 1,000 m down a single hillside, Tiger Leaping Gorge runs between two snow peaks 3,790 m above the water, and Pudacuo's lakes sit on a 3,700 m plateau, all inside one province.
because.exploration: Shaxi, Baisha, Azheke and the Erhai villages are ten to forty minutes off the tour-bus route and almost nobody goes, so a rented e-bike or a 20 CNY minibus changes your day completely.
because.food: Crossing-the-bridge noodles in Kunming, Bai sour-and-spicy fish and Xizhou baba around Erhai, Naxi chickpea jelly in Lijiang, yak and matsutake in Shangri-La, and from June to September the wild mushroom markets are the best eating in China
because.relaxation: Shaxi and the Erhai west shore are genuinely quiet, and Pu'er tea is served slowly everywhere, but the drive days are long and the altitude is not restful.
because.culture: Naxi, Bai, Hani, Yi and Tibetan in one route, with living writing at Baisha, a working Gelugpa monastery at Songzanlin and market days that are still markets rather than shows.
because.adventure: The Tiger Leaping Gorge high trail is two real days with 900 m of climbing, and Jade Dragon's cable car puts you at 4,506 m in eleven minutes whether your lungs are ready or not.
because.city: Kunming is pleasant and mild and almost entirely modern, so give it a day and a night market, not three days.

destination.caveat: The three famous old towns are the weakest part of the trip: Lijiang was rebuilt after the 1996 earthquake and is now largely souvenir shops, Dali's Fuxing Road is the same at half the scale, and Shangri-La's Dukezong burned down in January 2014 and what stands is a twelve-year-old replica, so plan  Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Kunming
cities.base: Around Green Lake and Wenlin Street, next to Yunnan University: the only part of Kunming with trees, coffee and food worth walking to, and a flat twenty minutes from the metro to the airport train.

cities.name: Yuanyang (Xinjie and the Hani villages)
cities.base: Sleep in Duoyishu village rather than Xinjie town if you can: the sunrise viewpoint is a ten minute walk instead of a forty minute drive in the dark, and the guesthouses there are simple but face the

cities.name: Dali
cities.base: Stay in a courtyard on the Cangshan side of the old town above Yeyu Road, or better, in a village on the Erhai shore at Caicun or Longkan; the old town's Renmin Road is loud until one in the morning.

cities.name: Shaxi
cities.base: Anywhere inside the walls around Sideng Square. The whole village is six streets and the converted courtyard inns are the best rooms on this route.

cities.name: Lijiang
cities.base: Sleep in Shuhe or at the quiet north end of Dayan near Black Dragon Pool. The blocks behind Sifang Street are bars and the noise runs past midnight.

cities.name: Shangri-La (Jiantang)
cities.base: The streets just north of Dukezong, near Beimen Street, so you can walk down into the old town and still be on a road a taxi can find. Ask for a room with a heater: it is 3,300 m and it is cold indoor

cities.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge
cities.base: The high trail has beds, at Tea Horse and Halfway and Tina's, but no town: you walk in from Qiaotou and out at Tina's, so this is a two day crossing hung off Lijiang, not a place you base yourself in.

cities.name: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
cities.base: No beds inside the scenic area worth having. Go out from Lijiang on the first shuttle at 07:30 and be back by mid afternoon, which is also when the cloud usually closes on the summit.

outings.name: Duoyishu sunrise
outings.why: The terraces face east and fill with mist that burns off between 07:30 and 09:00, and the viewing deck is the one place in Yuanyang that is genuinely crowded. From Xinjie it is a 40 minute drive in the dark on a road with no barrier; from D
outings.season: Water is in the terraces from mid November to early April an
outings.fallback: If it is flat grey, skip sunrise and walk the footpath down through Pugaolaozhai to Azheke instead, which is better in cloud.

outings.name: the Bada and Laohuzui sunset run
outings.why: Bada is the widest single sweep of terraces and Laohuzui is the steepest, and both face west, so this is an afternoon that ends in the dark. Laohuzui is another 40 minutes past Bada on a poor road and the last stretch is often being repaire
outings.season: All year. Cloud sits on the ridge most afternoons from June
outings.fallback: Stop at Bada, eat at the stalls in the car park, and drive back before dark rather than pushing on to Laohuzui.

outings.name: the Erhai east shore ride, Caicun to Xizhou
outings.why: A flat 25 km on the lakeside ecological corridor, which is closed to cars, through Longkan and Gusheng and Haishe to the Bai villages at Zhoucheng and Xizhou. Rent an e-bike, not a pedal bike, because the return leg is into the afternoon wi
outings.season: All year. March and April are windy, July and August bring a
outings.fallback: Ride only as far as Gusheng, 8 km, and take the bus back from the main road.

outings.name: the Cangshan Jade Belt Road
outings.why: Take the Gantong cableway up to about 2,600 m, then walk the Yudai (Jade Belt) path north along the contour with Erhai below you the whole way, and come down by the Zhonghe chairlift. Eleven kilometres, nearly flat, and the only hard part i
outings.season: All year. The cableways shut in high wind, which is most com
outings.fallback: Ride up and back on the Gantong cableway and walk the first 2 km of the path to Qingbi Stream.

outings.name: the Shaxi Friday market
outings.why: Bai and Yi farmers come down off the hills into Sideng Square and the surrounding lanes from about 07:00, and it is over by early afternoon. This is a market people buy pigs and fabric at, not a craft fair. It only happens on Friday, so the
outings.fallback: On any other day the square is quiet and the daily produce market beside the east gate is still worth half an hour.

outings.name: Shibaoshan
outings.why: Ninth and tenth century Nanzhao rock carvings cut into red sandstone at Shizhongshan, plus the cliff-hung Baoxiang Temple, 25 minutes north of Shaxi. It is stairs most of the way and about 400 m of climbing between the two sites.
outings.season: All year. The stone steps are slick after rain from June to
outings.fallback: Do the Shizhongshan grottoes only and skip Baoxiang Temple, which is the steep half.

outings.name: Glacier Park to 4,506 m
outings.why: A cable car from 3,356 m to 4,506 m in about eleven minutes, then a boardwalk staircase to 4,680 m. You gain 1,000 m without walking, so the headache is real and the stairs at the top are genuinely hard. Cable car tickets are capped daily a
outings.season: All year. The cable car closes in high wind and lightning, m
outings.fallback: Take the Yunshanping (Spruce Meadow) chairlift to 3,240 m instead, which is a flat meadow walk under the north face and needs no acclimatisation.

outings.name: Yunshanping and Blue Moon Valley
outings.why: The low half of the Jade Dragon scenic area: a chairlift to the spruce meadow at 3,240 m, then the shuttle down to the limestone pools of Baishuihe. Easy, but the shuttle bus queues at the Ganhaizi transfer point can run 40 minutes in high
outings.season: All year. The pools at Baishuihe are milky blue only when th
outings.fallback: Yuhu village and Joseph Rock's house at the mountain's foot, which needs no ticket queue.

outings.name: the 28 Bends, Qiaotou to Halfway
outings.why: Day one of the high trail. From the Qiaotou ticket office at 1,800 m up to the top of the 28 Bends at about 2,670 m, then a long traverse to Tea Horse or Halfway Guesthouse. The bends are the whole difficulty of the trek and they come in th
outings.season: All year. Avoid late June to August, when rockfall and mud o
outings.fallback: Take the bus to Tina's, walk the 30 minutes down to the Upper Gorge platform, and sleep at Halfway having driven the ridge road.

outings.name: Halfway to Tina's and the Middle Gorge ladders
outings.why: Day two. An easy 8 km of contouring and descent to Tina's, then the optional drop to the river at the Middle Gorge, which is 40 minutes down and an hour back up on cut steps and, if you want it, the vertical Sky Ladder. Local families charg
outings.season: All year. The river path floods and the ladders close during
outings.fallback: Walk to Tina's and take the afternoon bus to Shangri-La without going down to the water.

outings.name: Songzanlin morning
outings.why: The largest Tibetan monastery in Yunnan, 5 km out of town at 3,380 m, still housing several hundred monks. Go for the 08:00 to 09:30 chanting rather than the midday coach hour. It is a long stone staircase up to the main halls and at this a
outings.season: All year. The big masked dance festivals fall in the elevent
outings.fallback: Walk the lake path below the monastery, which gives the classic reflection view and needs no ticket.

outings.name: Pudacuo, Shudu Lake and Bita Lake
outings.why: Two plateau lakes at 3,600 to 3,700 m linked by park shuttle, with boardwalks of about 3 km at each. The walking is flat and the altitude still makes it feel like work. The full ticket is expensive by Chinese park standards and you are lock
outings.season: May to October for meadow flowers, late October for larch co
outings.fallback: Napahai, twenty minutes from town, free to walk the causeway edge, with cranes from November to March.

outings.name: Shilin, the Stone Forest
outings.why: Karst pinnacles 90 km east of Kunming, reachable in under an hour on the high speed train to Shilin West plus a shuttle. The Greater Stone Forest is a walled crowd; walk 25 minutes out to the Naigu black stone forest, which almost nobody do
outings.season: All year. Torch Festival in the sixth lunar month, usually l
outings.fallback: Yuantong Temple and the Zhuanxin produce market in Kunming, which is a better day than a wet Shilin.

places.name: Green Lake Park (Cuihu)
places.note: Free, and from November to March it fills with black-headed gulls that fly down from Siberia, which is the one time of year the park is genuinely worth crossing town for.

places.name: Yunnan Provincial Museum
places.note: Free with passport at the desk, shut on Mondays, last entry 16:00, and the Dian Kingdom bronzes on the second floor are the reason to go: they are 2,000 years old and look nothing like Han China.

places.name: Yuantong Temple
places.note: Tang foundation, Qing buildings, and unusual for a Chinese temple in that you walk down into it rather than up; the ticket is a few yuan and the incense smoke is thick on the first and fifteenth of the lunar month.

places.name: Jianxin Yuan crossing-the-bridge noodles
places.note: The old Kunming house for guoqiao mixian: a bowl of chicken broth under a film of oil arrives so hot it will cook raw pork, and you add the plates in order, meat first, greens and noodles last, or you get a cold bowl.

places.name: Zhuanxin produce market
places.note: A working wet market, not a tourist street, and from June to September a third of it is wild mushrooms: matsutake, milk caps and the blue-bruising jianshouqing that has to be cooked through or it makes you hallucinate.

places.name: Dounan flower market
places.note: Asia's largest fresh-cut flower auction, and it runs at night: the trading floor gets going after about 19:00 and roses sell by the armful for the price of a coffee, but it is a 45 minute metro ride each way.

places.name: Western Hills and the Dragon Gate
places.note: Grottoes cut by one monk over seventy years into a cliff above Dianchi, reached by chairlift or a long stair; the lake below is green with algae most of the year, so come for the rock passages rather than the water.

places.name: Golden Temple (Jindian)
places.note: A 1602 hall cast entirely in bronze, over 200 tonnes of it, in a camellia garden that flowers in February; quiet on a weekday and close to nothing else, so pair it with the flower market run.

places.name: Wenlin Street cafes
places.note: Yunnan grows most of China's coffee and this student street is where it gets roasted properly; ask for a Baoshan or Pu'er single origin rather than the sweetened latte everyone orders.

places.name: Guandu Ancient Town
places.note: Skip it: the Jingang Pagoda is genuinely 15th century but the lanes around it were flattened and rebuilt as a shopping street in the 2000s, and you will see the same souvenirs four more times this trip.

places.name: Yunnan Nationalities Village
places.note: Skip it: twenty-six ethnic groups played by costumed staff on a timetable, when in nine days you will be standing in real Bai, Naxi, Hani and Tibetan villages for free.

places.name: Shilin Stone Forest
places.note: Limestone pinnacles up to 30 m high and a UNESCO listing, but the Greater Stone Forest at the entrance is a slow-moving queue in flag-following groups; walk twenty-five minutes out to Naigu and you will have black karst to yourself.

places.name: Duoyishu sunrise deck
places.note: The east-facing amphitheatre everyone photographs, and the 100 CNY area ticket covers it for several days; the mist usually lifts between 07:30 and 09:00 and the deck is shoulder to shoulder with tripods by then.

places.name: Bada terraces
places.note: The widest single sweep of terraces on the mountain and it faces west, so it is a sunset stop; the area ticket bought at Duoyishu covers it, and the stalls in the car park grill decent river fish.

places.name: Laohuzui (Tiger's Mouth) terraces
places.note: The steepest and least regular of the three viewpoints and the best light of the day lands here, but it is another 40 minutes of poor road past Bada and the drive back is in full dark.

places.name: Azheke Hani village
places.note: Sixty-odd thatched mushroom houses run under a village-owned tourism scheme that pays residents to keep living there, so it is still a farming village and the small ticket goes to the households rather than a company.

places.name: Qingkou Hani folk village
places.note: The village closest to Xinjie and the one the tour buses stop at, so parts of it are performing for you; the terraced water channels and the sacred grove above the houses are the real thing and explain how the whole system works.

places.name: Shengcun market
places.note: Hani and Yi women come in from the ridges in indigo and silver and it is the best thing in Yuanyang on the right day, but it runs on a rolling multi-day cycle rather than a weekday, so ask your guesthouse the night before which village has market tomorrow.

places.name: Xinjie morning market
places.note: Daily, unglamorous and useful: this is where you buy breakfast, a rain poncho and the red rice that only grows in these terraces, and it is over by lunchtime.

places.name: Hani home cooking in Duoyishu
places.note: Guesthouse kitchens cook terrace red rice, loquat-leaf egg, cured pork and whatever green is up that week; order at breakfast for dinner because they shop for it during the day.

places.name: The Hani long-table feast
places.note: Changjiexuan is the Hani new year feast, hundreds of metres of tables down a village street, and it falls in the tenth lunar month, usually late November or December; outside that window what you are offered is a staged version for coaches.

places.name: Jianshui grilled tofu stalls
places.note: Small cubes of fermented tofu grilled over charcoal and counted with corn kernels as you eat; it comes from Jianshui up the road and it is the cheapest good thing in southern Yunnan.

places.name: Fuxing Road and the old town gates
places.note: Free to enter and worth exactly one early walk: the street plan and the Ming walls are real, almost every shopfront on them now sells rose cake and tie-dye, and by ten in the morning it is solid with tour groups.

places.name: Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple
places.neighborhood: North of the old town, under Cangshan
places.note: The tallest pagoda is 9th century Nanzhao work and has stood through earthquakes that flattened everything around it; the vast temple complex climbing the hill behind was built from nothing in 2005, so see the pagodas and the reflecting pool and do not feel obliged to walk the rest.

places.name: The Erhai ecological corridor at Caicun
places.neighborhood: Caicun, east of the old town
places.note: A car-free path running most of the way round the lake, built when the shoreline guesthouses were demolished for pollution control; rent an e-bike at Caicun, ride north, and turn back before the afternoon wind gets up.

places.name: Yan Family Compound, Xizhou
places.note: A 1920s Bai merchant house of linked courtyards with a whitewashed screen wall painted in ink, and the best explanation anywhere of what tea-caravan money bought; the museum rooms upstairs are thin, the building is not.

places.name: Xizhou baba at the market stalls
places.note: A layered wheat flatbread baked between charcoal above and below, sweet with rose sugar or savoury with pork and spring onion; buy it at the stall in the square where the queue is local and eat it standing up.

places.name: Shaping Monday market
places.note: Mondays only, and the reason to organise your Dali days around a Monday: Bai villagers trade livestock, tools, herbs and cloth from dawn, and it thins out badly after noon.

places.name: Gantong cableway and the Jade Belt Road
places.note: Up to about 2,600 m by cable, then a nearly flat 11 km contour path with Erhai a thousand metres below you the whole way; ticket sales stop mid afternoon and the cableways shut in wind, so start before ten.

places.name: Dali Museum
places.note: Free, shut Mondays, housed in the compound of Du Wenxiu who ruled Dali during the Panthay Rebellion; small, quiet, and the Nanzhao and Dali Kingdom stonework gives the Three Pagodas their context.

places.name: Bai sour and spicy fish at the lake villages
places.note: Erhai carp cooked in a clay pot with pickled bamboo, green chilli and a lot of sour, eaten with a side plate of raw vegetables; lake fish is farmed now, wild netting has been banned for years, and any menu claiming otherwise is lying.

places.name: Renmin Road bars
places.note: Dali has been the drop-out town of southwest China since the 1990s and the top of Renmin Road is still guitars and cheap beer and people who came for a week in 2019; loud enough that you should not sleep on it.

places.name: Shuanglang
places.note: Skip it: a fishing village rebuilt end to end as lakefront photo hotels, with a ninety minute drive each way and a queue for every jetty; the west shore villages at Gusheng and Zhoucheng are what Shuanglang was.

places.name: Bai three-course tea performance
places.note: Skip it: bitter, sweet and aftertaste tea is a genuine Bai custom, but the versions sold to visitors are a costumed floor show with a hard sell on tea bricks at the end.

places.name: Sideng Square and the theatre stage
places.note: The last intact caravan market square on the tea horse road, put on the World Monuments Watch list in 2001 and restored with Swiss help rather than demolished and rebuilt, which is exactly why it feels different from Lijiang.

places.name: Xingjiao Temple
places.note: A Ming Buddhist hall of 1415 with wall paintings that mix Chinese, Tibetan and Nanzhao figures, and a caretaker who will unlock the upper gallery if you ask; the light inside is poor after four in the afternoon.

places.name: The Friday market
places.neighborhood: Sideng Square and the east gate lanes
places.note: Friday only, and it is the single reason to fix your dates: Bai and Yi farmers walk down from the hills to sell pigs, hemp cloth, herbs and copper, and it is finished by early afternoon.

places.name: Yujin Bridge
places.neighborhood: Heihui River, east of the village
places.note: The 1867 stone arch the mule caravans crossed to leave for Tibet, still the village's way over the river; go at dusk when the swallows are out and the fields behind it are empty.

places.name: Shizhongshan grottoes, Shibaoshan
places.note: Nanzhao kingdom figures carved into red sandstone in the 9th and 10th centuries, including a Persian-featured foreigner and a frankly explicit fertility carving that local women still make offerings to; it is all steps, and slippery in rain.

places.name: Baoxiang Temple
places.note: A temple pinned to a vertical cliff face, reached by a stair cut into the rock and covered by the same Shibaoshan ticket; the macaques on the path will go through an open bag in seconds.

places.name: The old caravan trail to Mapingguan
places.neighborhood: West of Shaxi, toward the pass
places.note: Two or three hours of flagstone and dirt up the valley on the actual road the mule trains took toward the Mekong, with hoof-worn stone in places; no signs in English and no water on the way, so carry it.

places.name: Ouyang Courtyard
places.note: A Qing caravan merchant's house of three courtyards still lived in by the family, with the stables on the ground floor; knock rather than walk in, and the small fee is paid at the door.

places.name: Bai courtyard dinner in Sideng
places.note: Most of the inns cook one set dinner from what came in that morning: cured ham, stir-fried mountain greens, river snails, a clay pot of chicken with wild pepper; tell them by mid afternoon or the kitchen has closed.

places.name: Coffee on Sideng Square
places.note: Three or four small places under the old arcades roast Yunnan beans and are run by people who moved here from Shanghai a decade ago; it is the right place to sit out the hour when the day trippers from Dali arrive.

places.name: Old Town maintenance fee desk
places.neighborhood: Dayan, checkpoints at Mufu and Black Dragon Pool
places.note: The ancient city maintenance fee, currently 50 CNY per person, is not collected at the town gates but at Mufu, Black Dragon Pool, Wangu Tower and the Jade Dragon ticket office, so budget it once, keep the receipt, and it covers the whole stay.

places.name: Mu Family Mansion (Mufu)
places.neighborhood: West edge of Dayan, under Lion Hill
places.note: The compound of the Naxi chieftains who ran this valley for four hundred years, rebuilt in the 1990s on the original footprint with 1998 money; the hillside courtyards climb well and the maintenance fee is checked at this gate.

places.name: Lion Hill and Wangu Tower
places.note: A cheap ticket and the only place you see the grey tile roofs as a whole with Jade Dragon behind them; go at seven, before the roofs fill with drone noise and the tour flags arrive.

places.name: Black Dragon Pool (Jade Spring Park)
places.note: Free in itself but the maintenance fee is checked at the gate, and the postcard reflection of the mountain in the pool only works on a still morning; in dry spring years the spring has run low and the pool has been part empty.

places.name: Baisha murals and Baisha village
places.note: Fifteenth century wall paintings in the Dabaoji Palace where Naxi, Tibetan and Chinese Buddhist figures share the same panel, and the village outside is still the old Naxi capital rather than a shopping street; this is the part of Lijiang worth your time.

places.name: Zhongyi Market
places.note: Inside the old town but for residents, not visitors: Naxi grandmothers selling mountain herbs, cured pork, walnut oil and in autumn baskets of matsutake graded by size in front of you.

places.name: Naxi chickpea jelly and baba
places.note: Jidou liangfen is a chickpea jelly served cold with chilli and vinegar in summer or fried in slabs in winter, and Naxi baba is a fried flaky flatbread with ham; both cost small change at the market stalls and triple on Sifang Street.

places.name: Dongba Culture Museum
places.note: Dongba is the last pictographic script still in liturgical use anywhere, and this is the one place that explains it properly rather than selling you a painted bookmark of your name in it.

places.name: Shuhe Old Town
places.note: Free now that its own ticket was dropped, older water channels than Dayan and perhaps a third of the crowds, but the same bars and silver shops are moving in year by year; better as a place to sleep than as a sight.

places.name: Naxi ancient music concert
places.note: Tang and Song court tunes kept alive by a Naxi orchestra, and it was remarkable when the players were men in their eighties who had hidden the instruments through the Cultural Revolution; most of those men have died and what is left is a competent recital at tourist prices.

places.name: Sifang Street and the bar lanes
places.note: Skip it: the heart of the old town after the 1996 earthquake rebuild is now competing sound systems and drink-and-shout bars, and it is the single clearest picture of what mass tourism did to Lijiang.

places.name: Songzanlin Monastery
places.note: Founded 1679, wrecked in the Cultural Revolution, rebuilt from 1983 and now home to several hundred Gelugpa monks; the ticket price has been cut twice in recent years so confirm it at the window, and the long stair to the main halls at 3,380 m will make you stop.

places.name: Pudacuo National Park
places.neighborhood: Shudu and Bita lakes, 22 km east
places.note: Two plateau lakes at 3,600 to 3,700 m joined by compulsory shuttle, with about 3 km of boardwalk at each; expensive, tightly controlled, and the flat walking still feels like effort at this height.

places.name: Napahai
places.note: A seasonal lake that floods in the summer rains and drains to grazing marsh the rest of the year, with black-necked cranes and bar-headed geese on it from November to March; you can walk the causeway edge for free and skip the ticketed horse paddocks.

places.name: Dukezong old town lanes
places.neighborhood: Dukezong, south of the modern town
places.note: Skip the shopping lanes: the fire of 11 January 2014 destroyed about 242 buildings and half the old town, and what you walk through now is a twelve-year-old timber replica full of the same yak-jerky and silver shops as Lijiang.

places.name: Guishan Temple prayer wheel
places.note: The wheel is 21 m high and takes a dozen people to turn, and it survived the 2014 fire; go at dusk when Tibetan residents walk the kora clockwise around it, which is a real evening habit rather than a performance.

places.name: Shika Snow Mountain cable car
places.note: Cable car from 3,200 m to about 4,450 m with a boardwalk along the ridge and, on a clear day, a line of snow peaks north to Meili; that is a 1,250 m gain in twenty minutes, so do it on your second day here, not your first.

places.name: Jiantang farmers market
places.note: Yak butter in cloth, dried matsutake by the kilo, barley flour, cordyceps under glass and hard curd cheese; in August the fresh mushroom trade here supplies the exporters who fly them to Tokyo overnight.

places.name: Yak hotpot and matsutake
places.note: Yak bone broth, yak meat, highland potatoes and mountain greens, and from late June to September thin slices of matsutake dropped in raw; it is the warmest room you will find in a town where indoor heating is mostly a rumour.

places.name: Butter tea and zanba
places.note: Salted yak butter tea and roasted barley flour kneaded in the bowl with your fingers; it tastes like hot savoury broth rather than tea, and it is the standard local answer to a bad altitude morning.

places.name: Tianshengqiao hot springs
places.note: Basic concrete pools fed by a genuine hot spring in a river gorge, used mostly by Tibetan families rather than visitors; do not expect a spa, and do not go on your first afternoon at altitude.

places.name: Tibetan family visit dinner show
places.note: Skip it: the zangmin jiafang evenings are coach parties in a purpose-built hall with barley wine, a dance circle and a sales pitch on silver and cordyceps at the end.

places.name: Qiaotou ticket office and trailhead
places.note: The gorge entrance fee is currently around 45 to 50 CNY and is checked again further along the trail, so keep the ticket; luggage can be left here or forwarded to Tina's for a small fee, which is what almost everyone does.

places.name: The 28 Bends
places.neighborhood: High trail above Qiaotou, up to 2,670 m
places.note: The switchbacks that make or break day one: roughly 500 m of climbing in under two hours with no shade, and locals wait at the bottom with horses at a price that rises with how tired you look.

places.name: Naxi Family Guesthouse
places.note: The standard first stop, about two hours in and just before the climb; eat here rather than after the bends, and fill both water bottles because there is nothing on the switchbacks.

places.name: Tea Horse Guesthouse
places.note: The first place with beds after the bends and the quieter of the two overnight options; rooms are simple, hot water depends on the solar tank, and it is about an hour short of Halfway.

places.name: Halfway Guesthouse
places.note: The obvious night one stop, with the open-air terrace looking straight across at Jade Dragon's west face and the famously unwalled toilet view; book ahead from October, because it fills.

places.name: Tina's Guesthouse and the road exit
places.note: Where the high trail drops back to the road and where buses to Shangri-La and Lijiang pick up in the early afternoon; it is a transit point with a restaurant, not a destination, so do not plan a night here.

places.name: The Middle Gorge and the Sky Ladder
places.note: Forty minutes of cut steps down to the water where the river funnels through the narrows, then an hour back up; the local families who maintain the paths charge cash at the top, and the Sky Ladder is a near-vertical steel ladder that is not for anyone unhappy with exposure.

places.name: Walnut Garden
places.neighborhood: Lower road, east end of the gorge
places.note: The hamlet past Tina's with the older guesthouses, Sean's and Chateau de Woody, where trekkers used to spend a second night before the road was improved; still the best dinner in the gorge and the quietest place to sleep in it.

places.name: Upper Gorge Tiger Leaping Stone platform
places.neighborhood: Upper gorge, river level below the road
places.note: The boulder in the river the tiger is supposed to have jumped, reached by escalator and concrete stairs from the road, and this is the version coach tours do in an hour; the water is genuinely loud and the crowd is genuinely heavy.

places.name: Haba Snow Mountain from the high trail
places.note: You walk the whole high trail on Haba's flank at 5,396 m with Jade Dragon at 5,596 m across the river, and the 3,790 m of relief between peak and water is what makes this one of the deepest gorges on earth.

places.name: Glacier Park cable car to 4,506 m
places.neighborhood: Jade Dragon scenic area, main cableway
places.note: Eleven minutes from 3,356 m to 4,506 m, then a boardwalk stair to 4,680 m that most people climb in short bursts; daily tickets are capped and sell out, so book the day before, and the cable car stops in wind and lightning.

places.name: Yunshanping (Spruce Meadow)
places.neighborhood: Jade Dragon scenic area, east chairlift
places.note: A chairlift to a spruce meadow at 3,240 m directly under the north face, flat walking on boardwalk and no altitude problem; this is the sensible substitute when the main cable car is sold out or shut.

places.name: Maoniuping (Yak Meadow)
places.neighborhood: Jade Dragon scenic area, south chairlift
places.note: The least visited of the three lifts, up to about 3,700 m, with yaks actually grazing and a small Tibetan chapel on the meadow; often empty on a weekday while the other two queue.

places.name: Blue Moon Valley and Baishuihe
places.note: Terraced limestone pools that are milky turquoise when the flow is low, roughly November to May, and grey meltwater in the summer rains; the boardwalk is short and packed, so go late in the day.

places.name: Impression Lijiang
places.note: Zhang Yimou's outdoor spectacle with several hundred villagers and horses and the mountain as backdrop, running one or two afternoon shows; it is a big loud pageant rather than anything Naxi, and at 3,100 m in the open you will want a coat and a hat.

places.name: Ganhaizi meadow and the shuttle transfer
places.note: The dry lake meadow where every shuttle in the park changes over, which means the best free view of the whole range and, in high season, a forty minute bus queue you cannot avoid.

places.name: Oxygen and coat rental at the cableway base
places.note: Canned oxygen and a rented down coat are sold at every stall and both are cheaper in Lijiang town the night before; the oxygen helps a little and does not make 4,680 m safe if you flew in from sea level two days ago.

places.name: Yuhu village and Joseph Rock's house
places.note: A cobbled Naxi village of volcanic stone where the botanist Joseph Rock lived through the 1920s and 1930s and sent the plant collections and the National Geographic articles that made this valley known abroad; quiet, cheap, and outside the main ticket gates.

places.name: Lanyue Valley boardwalk
places.note: The kilometre of boardwalk above the pools that most groups turn back before reaching, so it thins out fast; covered by the scenic area ticket and the best chance of a photograph without forty people in it.

places.name: Jade Water Village (Yushuizhai)
places.neighborhood: Below Baisha, on the Jade Dragon road
places.note: Skip it: a built Dongba theme site of pools, totems and costumed staff on the way to the mountain, sold as a cultural stop by drivers who get a commission for taking you.
